The Dune Camp | Safari Lodge Properties | Bush Ways Botswana
Kalahari / Deception Valley Private Reserve
The Dune Camp
The Deception Valley Private Reserve spans 43,000-hectares of pristine Kalahari wilderness.
Into the Red Kalahari
Dune Camp, nestled the north-eastern boundary of the Central Kalahari Game Reserve in one of the largest private game reserves in Botswana. The Deception Valley Private Reserve spans 43,000-hectares of pristine Kalahari wilderness. Designated waterholes, hidden viewing hides, vegetated dunes, natural pans and an amazing valley offering incredible game viewing opportunities. The lodge uniquely pairs traditional safaris with cultural immersion, as guests are guided through traditional activities by the Naru-speaking San tribe’s. During day and night game drives, witness diverse wildlife including the black-maned Kalahari lion, cheetah, and elusive species like the brown hyena and pangolin. Explore the bush on foot to uncover Bushman hunting techniques and traditions. Accessible by air or road, the lodge boasts eight spacious suites overlooking the African savanna.
experiences at this lodge
Game Drives
Our guided game drives provide the opportunity to explore diverse wilderness areas with experienced professional guides. Guests encounter a wide range of wildlife while learning about animal behaviour, ecosystems, and the rhythms of the bush. Each drive delivers a unique and immersive safari experience shaped by the landscape and the moment.
San Trail Nature Walk
Experience a cultural encounter at Deception Valley Private Reserve with the San Bushmen, descendants of Southern Africa’s earliest inhabitants. Join a guided walk to learn about their tracking skills, medicinal plant knowledge, and deep connection to the Kalahari, gaining insight into one of the world’s oldest living cultures.

Where our camps and lodges are
Botswana’s safari regions can feel remarkably different from one another. Our camps and lodges are spread across contrasting landscapes, making it possible to choose a stay that suits the kind of wildlife and wilderness experience you are looking for.
Okavango Delta, Khwai & Moremi
The Okavango is a river that never reaches the sea, spreading into channels and floodplains where the wildlife moves with the water. Khwai and Moremi sit along its eastern edge. Elephant, buffalo, lion, leopard and wild dog are all present, though nothing is ever guaranteed. Sango Safari Camp sits on the Khwai floodplains; Khwai Guest House is in the village itself.
Explore More
Chobe & Mababe
Chobe is best known for its elephants, which gather along the river in large numbers through the dry months. Mababe is quieter - a private concession bordering the park, with far fewer vehicles. Chobe Elephant Camp overlooks the floodplains; Mababe Tented Camp sits on the riverbank.
Explore More
Kalahari & Makgadikgadi
The south is dry, open and far less visited. Deception Valley Lodge and The Dune Camp sit within a 43,000-hectare private reserve on the edge of the Central Kalahari, where the wildlife is desert-adapted and the silence stays with you. Boteti River Camp overlooks one of Makgadikgadi’s most important water sources, where zebra return in large numbers as the surrounding pans dry.

About Us | Expert Safari Guides | Bush Ways Botswana
Who are we?
About Us
For thirty years, Bush Ways Botswana has specialised in curating authentic safari experiences that prioritise wilderness, authenticity, conservation, and exceptional guiding. Our journeys go beyond sightseeing - connecting travellers to Botswana’s ecosystems, cultures, and remote places in a way that feels honest and immersive.
Home About Us
Our ethos
Ethos
At Bush Ways Botswana, we believe safari is not simply about travel. It is about connection. Connection to the land, to wildlife, to community, and to one another.
For three decades, we have remained proudly wilderness and conservation driven. Our story began with a deep respect for the African bush and a belief that authentic safari experiences should be personal, purposeful, and profoundly moving.
We are not just a safari company, we are a clan!
History
Scroll
June 1996
Beginning of an Adventure
Since 1996, Bush Ways has proudly delivered “Adventure Journeys to the Heart of Africa.” What began as a passionate vision has grown into a respected and recognised name in Botswana’s tourism landscape, built on authenticity, experience, and a deep love for the wild.
April 1997
The Genesis on Wheels
Armed with a single vehicle, a spirit of adventure, and a dream to share Botswana’s untamed beauty, Bush Ways began as a small guiding operation. Today, that same passion drives our commitment to authentic safari experiences, exceptional value, and responsible, sustainable tourism.
July 2010
Sango Safari Camp
Bush Ways opened Sango Safari Camp in the Khwai region of the Okavango Delta, marking its first permanent safari camp. This milestone expanded the company from mobile safaris into lodge-based experiences within one of Botswana’s richest wildlife areas.
Why Bush Ways?
At Bush Ways Botswana, we don’t just take guests into the bush, but we invite them into our world. With over 30 years of guiding through Botswana’s wilderness, our safaris are rooted in deep local knowledge, genuine hospitality, and a passion for authentic encounters lived with our expert nature guides.
Our guides are storytellers, trackers, and conservation custodians. Our camps are intimate and immersive, and our experiences are shaped around the rhythm of nature.
Why Bush Ways
Our Fleet
Bush Ways operates a fleet of 70 vehicles, including 14 specialised safari vehicles purpose-built for Botswana’s remote terrain. Designed for optimal wildlife viewing, photography, and off-road performance, they feature elevated seating, open viewing access, charging points, and reinforced suspension. Supported by a wider operational fleet, our vehicles ensure reliability, independence, and seamless safaris, allowing close guide interaction and immersive bush experiences.
Our Fleet
The Bush Ways Clan
Meet the team
One of our greatest strengths lies behind the scenes.
Over the years, we have built one of the strongest mobile safari set-ups and support centres in the region; a solid operational backbone that allows every Bush Ways safari to run seamlessly from start to finish.
Situated on 2,000 square metres at the entrance of Maun, our headquarters is the engine room of our operations. From here, your journey is carefully managed from the moment your booking is confirmed and often long after your safari ends.
In the background, our fully equipped professional workshop is supervised by our Technical Operations Manager and a dedicated team of mechanics. They build, maintain, and service our vehicles and safari equipment to the highest standard. We even have our own in-house tailor ensuring tents, canvas, and custom fittings are always field-ready.
This integrated support structure allows us to operate independently and efficiently in some of Botswana’s most remote wilderness areas, delivering safaris that feel effortless to our guests, because every detail has already been thought through.
HQ Team
Our team includes:
-Reservations, Sales & Marketing, ensuring clear communication, tailored planning, and personalised service.
-Accounts & Administration, maintaining efficiency and accuracy
-Operations Specialists, meticulously coordinating logistics so that every element of your safari is controlled pre-, during, and post-travel
Marc Germiquet
Director
Marc Germiquet is the Founder and Director of Bush Ways Safaris. After beginning his guiding career in 1991, he established Bush Ways in 1996 with a vision to deliver authentic, quality-driven safari experiences. Marc combines a passion for wilderness, strong operational leadership, and a deep commitment to community development across Botswana shown through Bush Ways Foundation.
Heiko Genzmer
Director
Heiko Genzmer is a Director of Bush Ways Safaris, bringing over three decades of safari and expedition experience. Since joining the company in the late 1990s, he has helped grow its mobile safari operations and strengthen field logistics. Heiko’s practical expertise and love for the African bush ensure seamless, well-executed adventures.
Mark Swaffield
Director
Mark Swaffield is a Director at Bush Ways Safaris, contributing extensive experience in safari logistics and field operations. He plays a key role in maintaining the company’s mobile safari infrastructure and operational standards, ensuring seamless experiences in Botswana’s remote wilderness areas. His hands-on approach and passion for the bush underpin every well-executed safari.
Nicola Hawes
Director
Nicola Hawes is a Managing Director at Bush Ways Safaris, overseeing finance, administration, and organisational development. She ensures the company’s systems run efficiently and sustainably, supporting smooth coordination between reservations, accounts, and field teams. Nicola’s leadership strengthens the operational foundation that allows Bush Ways to deliver consistently professional and reliable safari experiences.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) | Bush Ways Botswana
Safari Planning FAQS
Find answers to common questions about travelling in Botswana, from packing and logistics to how our safaris operate.
Explore Botswana
Planning Your Journey
Planning a safari to Botswana comes with plenty of questions - from what to pack and when to travel, to how our mobile camps work. Below you’ll find practical guidance to help you prepare, along with common frequently asked questions drawn from decades of guiding experience.
What to pack
Resources

Bush Ways Adventure Camping Safari Guest Info
Can I bring my children?
What vaccinations do I need?

Can I bring my children?
Yes, you can
Children are welcome on many of our safaris, however minimum age requirements vary depending on the itinerary and style of safari. For mobile camping departures, we generally recommend children be aged 12 and above due to the nature of long game drives and remote camp environments. Private departures offer greater flexibility and can be tailored to families travelling with younger children. Please speak with our team to determine the most suitable option.
What vaccinations do I need?
None are required but vaccinations are recommended
Travellers should consult their doctor or travel clinic well in advance of departure. Botswana is a low-risk destination in terms of required vaccinations, however routine travel immunisations are recommended. Malaria is present in northern Botswana (including the Okavango Delta and surrounding areas), so anti-malarial medication is typically advised. Requirements can vary depending on your country of origin and any transit countries, particularly regarding yellow fever certificates.
What should I pack?
Minimal luggage is recommended
Soft-sided luggage is essential, as light aircraft transfers have strict weight limits (typically 20kg including hand luggage). Neutral-coloured, lightweight clothing is recommended for game drives, along with a warm layer for early mornings in winter (May–August). Comfortable closed shoes, sun protection, a hat and binoculars are all useful. Detailed packing guidance is provided prior to departure to ensure you’re fully prepared.
When is the best time to visit Botswana?
All year round
Botswana is a year-round safari destination, with each season offering a different experience.
May–October (Dry Season): Cooler temperatures and concentrated wildlife around water sources make this the peak game-viewing period.
November–April (Green Season): Lush landscapes, dramatic skies and excellent birdlife define this time of year. It’s also when many animals give birth, offering unique wildlife interactions.
The best time depends on what you most want to experience — our team can guide you based on your interests.
How much does a Botswana safari cost?
It can vary
Botswana is considered one of Africa’s more exclusive safari destinations due to its low-volume, high-conservation tourism model. Prices vary depending on safari style (Adventure Camping, Premium Camping or Lodge-to-Lodge), duration and season. As a general guide, mobile safaris typically start from mid-range pricing and increase with added comfort and private departures. For an accurate quotation, we recommend reviewing specific itineraries or requesting tailored pricing based on your travel dates.
Do they speak english in Botswana?
Yes
English is the official language of Botswana and is widely spoken throughout the country. It is used in government, tourism and education. In addition, Setswana is the national language, and many of our guides speak multiple local dialects alongside fluent English.
Where to fly into Botswana for a safari​?
Maun or Kasane depending on the safari
Most international travellers fly into Maun (MUB), the gateway to the Okavango Delta and northern safari regions. Some itineraries may also begin in Kasane (BBK), particularly those exploring Chobe National Park. Both airports are well connected via Johannesburg, which serves as the primary international hub for southern Africa. From Maun or Kasane, light aircraft transfers are typically used to access remote safari are.
Visa Advice
Visa requirements for Botswana vary depending on your nationality. Many travellers from the United Kingdom, United States, European Union, Canada and Australia do not require a visa for short tourist stays. However, entry requirements can change, so we always recommend checking with your local Botswana High Commission or official government website before travelling.
Your passport must be valid for at least six months beyond your date of departure and should have at least three blank pages for entry stamps. Proof of onward or return travel may also be requested upon arrival.
If your journey involves transiting through another country - most commonly South Africa - please ensure you also meet their entry requirements, including any transit visa regulations. Travellers arriving from, or passing through, a yellow fever risk country may be required to present a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate.
We provide detailed pre-departure information prior to travel to ensure you are aware of all current requirements relevant to your itinerary.
